metadata.title: Exit times in non-Markovian drifting continuous-time random walk processes

extraction_notes.note: The sentence introducing $\varrho$ lies inside the prose renewal argument PP2 but $\varrho$ is used throughout the paper, so it is a definition node nested in the proof rather than only a step.
One sentence both introduces $\mu$, $\mu_r$ (used later) and states the small-$v$ expansion; kept as a single claim since nodes never split a sentence.
Numbered equation (3) is named 'the integral renewal equation', so retyped as an external theorem rather than an equation.
Worked Erlang/exponential cases are long computations with many numbered equations; each kept as one example node with nested equations rather than splitting every derivation sentence into claims.
Introduction motivation, Conclusions summary and figure captions were not extracted; the unnumbered inverse-Laplace display in Section 4 stays inside ExP2.
Label hat_phi sits on a subequations block that latex_facts maps to no fact, so refs to it were added by hand as named edges from ClP2.

nodes.statement: All through this paper we will assume that (i) the sojourn times tau_n>0 are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) random variables with probability density and cumulative distribution function (PDF and, respectively, CDF) psi(t) and Psi(t)= int_0^t psi(t')d t'; (ii) \J_n\ is a sequence of i.i.d. random variables with common PDF h(cdot); and (iii), that J_m is independent of tau_n for any n,m.
nodes.raw_latex:
All through this paper  we will assume that (i) the
sojourn times $\tau_n>0$
 are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) random variables with
probability density and cumulative distribution function (PDF and,
respectively, CDF) $\psi(t)$ and $\Psi(t)=  \int_0^t \psi(t')d
t'$; (ii) $\{J_n\}$ is a sequence of i.i.d. random variables  with
common PDF $h(\cdot)$; and  (iii), that  $ J_m$ is independent of $\tau_n $ for any $n,m$.

Here  we address these issues      and
generalize the  results of  \cite{mmp05,mmpw06} in a twofold way
by assuming  that   (i) a drift $vt>0$ operates on the system and

jump instant, and the observer \it  has  knowledge of the present,
but not of  the history, of the system\rm.

To this  end    let $r+\mathbf{t}_b^{x,r}$ be the first time past
$r$ at which $X_t$ exits $(0,b)$;   $T_{b}(x,r)$ be its expected
value: $T_{b}(x,r) =\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{t}_b^{x,r}]$; finally let
$\mathbb{T}_{b}(x) $ denote   the mean exit time   off $(0,b)$     after
a jump $t_n$ (loosely one has $\mathbb{T}_{b}(x)=T_{b}(x,t_n), n=0,\dots,
\infty$; however the relation between both   quantities is not
trivial, as we see below in Section~\ref{S_up}).
